question: What is the growth plan for Frontline?
html:
Frontline Managed Services growth plan

BSP's growth plan for Frontline has four phases over about 42 months. Frontline will earn more from each AM Law client, move down into mid-size firms, consolidate eBilling and accounts receivable, and then expand into the UK and Canada. Because entry was about 12-15x (est.) on a $90M term loan, EBITDA growth has to drive the return (Frontline growth plan; Frontline public filings).

Starting point

  • BSP closed the deal on Dec 9, 2024. Equity was about $137-150M and the NXT/Audax term loan was $90M (Frontline public filings).
  • Adjusted EBITDA at close was $16-20M (est.) on revenue of $100-140M (est.). Both figures are backed out from leverage and headcount, not company disclosures (Frontline public filings).
  • Frontline has about 1,100 staff and 900+ law-firm clients, including about half the AM Law 200. Tim Britt has been CEO since Jan 27, 2026 (BSP firm profile; Frontline growth plan).

Four phases

  • Phase 1 (months 0-12): AM Law upsell.
  • Rebuild HELIX as a product-led service desk with a Tier-0 AI agent.
  • Add a cyber-posture subscription and legal-AI enablement services.
  • The AI gap is large: 68% of firms have Copilot, but only 8% have deployed it firm-wide (Frontline growth plan).
  • Phase 2 (months 6-18): mid-size firms.
  • The target universe is 143 firms with 17,042 attorneys across 16 metros. Of these, 37 score 65 or higher on fit (Mid-size law firms).
  • The top three are Weber Gallagher (85), Evans & Dixon (83) and Rivkin Radler (82).
  • Local legal MSPs are acquisition candidates, for example Kraft Kennedy (about $21.5M revenue, est.) and Innovative Computing Systems (about $12.6M, est.) (Frontline and Thomas Scientific add-on targets).
  • Phase 3 (months 12-30): eBilling and AR.
  • Client-side AI has pushed invoice rejections from 11% to 18%.
  • The plan buys from a screen that includes Helm360, The Garver Group and The Legal Billing Group.
  • Four finance agents would be priced on days-to-pay (Frontline growth plan).
  • Phase 4 (months 24-42): UK and Canada.
  • Entry would be through acquired local providers such as Quiss, Accurate Legal Billing and CG Technologies (Frontline growth plan).

Targets (all estimates)

MonthRevenueEBITDAMarginHeadcountClients
0$130M$20M~15.4%1,150900
12$150M$25M~16.7%1,3001,000
24$180M$32M~17.8%1,5001,150
36$215M$41M~19%1,6501,300

Over three years this is about 1.65x revenue and about 2x EBITDA (est.). Roughly $55M of that revenue comes from acquisitions (est.) (Frontline growth plan).

Key risks

  • Every revenue and EBITDA figure above inherits low-to-medium confidence. Confirming the baseline needs the actual 2025 audited financials (Frontline public filings).
  • The ZoomInfo revenue figures for targets are directional only. Helm360's $116.5M (est.) is flagged as likely overstated (Frontline and Thomas Scientific add-on targets).
  • Debt capacity for acquisitions is unknown. Revolver, delayed-draw or incremental tranches have not been disclosed (Frontline public filings).

Next actions

  1. Replace the modelled baseline with management's trailing-twelve-month revenue, EBITDA and margin by service line, then re-run the KPI roadmap.
  2. Confirm available acquisition debt capacity with NXT and Audax before approaching Kraft Kennedy or Innovative Computing Systems.
  3. Build outreach plans for the 37 mid-size firms scoring 65 or higher, starting with the top five.
  4. Get verified revenue for the Phase 3 eBilling targets, starting with Helm360.
